name: Sully Balloo's Letter
summary: Sully Balloo's Letter carries a soldier's farewell from the waters beneath the Thandol Span. Addressed to his wife Sara in Ironforge, it bears the love that endured through his final days.

sections.title: A Final Farewell Beneath the Waves
sections.body: Beneath the Thandol Span, where the Wetlands road crosses toward the Arathi Highlands, a dwarf's skeletal remains lie pinned under rushing water. In his grasp rests a fragile, waterlogged envelope. The letter inside begins, “My dear Sara...” Its parchment has suffered beneath the water, but the ink still holds the care with which the dwarven defender wrote in his final days or hours. He never returned to Ironforge.

sections.title: Delivery to Ironforge
sections.body: In Ironforge, Sara Balloo has lived with the uncertainty of a wife whose husband marched off to war. Reading Sully's final thoughts brings somber closure and confirms her fear: he died far from home beneath the currents of the northern crossing. His devotion reaches her in his own words.

faq.q: Where is Sully Balloo's Letter found?
aliases: where to find sully balloo letter
faq.answer: You find the letter in a waterlogged envelope clutched in the hand of a skeletal dwarf beneath the waters of the Thandol Span, between the Wetlands and the Arathi Highlands.
Sully Balloo was a dwarven soldier who died near the Thandol Span while defending the northern crossing. His remains lie pinned beneath the river currents.

faq.q: Who is the letter addressed to?
aliases: where to turn in sully letter
faq.answer: The letter is addressed to Mrs. Sara Balloo, Sully's wife, who lives in Ironforge.

faq.q: What happens when you deliver the letter to Sara Balloo?
faq.answer: When Sara Balloo reads the letter, she is heartbroken to learn that her husband died beneath the waters. She can still read the final words he lovingly wrote to her.

angles.text: As a dwarf, you can see in the letter the sacrifice ordinary mountaineers and soldiers make while guarding Khaz Modan's high bridges and mountain passes.
As an Alliance member, you can help carry a fallen soldier's last thoughts to his widow, so they are not forgotten beneath the bridge.
